documents: Hydrogels whose stress relaxes quickly let encapsulated cells spread, proliferate and remodel their surroundings, whereas elastic gels of the same initial stiffness keep cells rounded. The effect depends on the timescale of relaxation relative to the time a cell takes to pull on its matrix.

We measured the viscoelastic moduli of alginate networks crosslinked with calcium at four molecular weights. Lower molecular weight chains relaxed stress faster, and adding short polyethylene glycol spacers widened the accessible range without changing the elastic modulus.

Patient-derived organoids reproduce many features of the tumour they came from, including drug response, but the reconstituted basement membrane they grow in varies from batch to batch and is poorly defined chemically.

Mitochondria can move between cells through tunnelling nanotubes and extracellular vesicles. Cancer cells that acquire mitochondria from neighbouring immune cells gain oxidative capacity, while the donor cells lose function.

Bayesian optimisation proposes the next experiment by balancing the predicted value of a formulation against the uncertainty of the surrogate model. With a Gaussian process and expected improvement, twenty rounds were enough to find adhesives stronger than any in the training set.

Bacteriophages inject their genome through the cell envelope in seconds. A membrane-anchored nuclease that sits near the injection site can cut the incoming DNA before it is protected by phage proteins.

The protein folds through a transition state in which a few native contacts have already formed; mutating those residues slows folding without changing stability, consistent with a nucleation-condensation mechanism.

Light-sheet microscopy images large cleared samples quickly, but scattering in dense tissue still blurs the sheet. Matching the refractive index of the medium to that of the tissue restores optical transparency.
A synthetic gene circuit that couples growth to a quorum-sensing signal keeps two strains at a set ratio in co-culture: when one strain overgrows, the signal it produces slows its own division.
